Where to Eat in Pomaire: Giant Empanadas, Restaurants and Prices 2026

Last updated: September 2026 | Reading time: 8 minutes

Pomaire is one of the great food destinations in central Chile. Just 50 minutes from Santiago, this pottery village is famous throughout the country for its giant empanada and for a hearty country cuisine that is cooked and served in clay pots and plates made by the village's own artisans. In this guide we tell you what to eat, where and at what prices in 2026.

In this guide

  • The giant empanada of Pomaire
  • Traditional dishes you must try
  • Reference prices 2026
  • How to choose a restaurant in Pomaire

The giant empanada of Pomaire

The giant baked empanada from the clay oven is the star dish of Pomaire and one of the reasons thousands of people visit the village every weekend. In 1995, Pomaire made the news for making the largest empanada in the world, a milestone that stayed in the collective memory and cemented the village's culinary fame.

The giant version served today by several restaurants weighs close to one kilo and is filled with the classic Chilean pino: beef, onion, hard-boiled egg, olive and raisins. It is a generous portion meant to be shared or for the very hungry. Its price is around $6,000 to $7,000 CLP depending on the restaurant and the filling.

Tip: The giant empanada is huge. If two of you also want to try a cazuela or a pastel de choclo, a single empanada to share is enough.

Traditional dishes you must try

  • Baked clay-oven empanada: The most famous in Chile. Crispy dough and a generous pino filling. Available in regular and giant size.
  • Beef cazuela: Served in a steaming clay pot with potato, squash, corn and a good piece of meat. A comforting classic.
  • Pastel de choclo: In an individual clay dish, with pino, a piece of chicken, olive and toasted sugar on top.
  • Humitas: Made from fresh corn, prepared home-style, ideal in the summer season.
  • Arrollado huaso and pork cuts: Hearty country cuisine for those looking for something filling.
  • Artisanal chicha: Made from grapes or apples, fermented the traditional way. The village's typical drink.

Reference prices 2026

These are approximate price ranges so you can plan your budget. They may vary depending on the restaurant and the season:

Dish / itemApprox. price (CLP)
Baked empanada (regular)$3,500 – $5,000
Giant empanada (~1 kg)$6,000 – $7,000
Beef cazuela in clay pot$7,000 – $10,000
Pastel de choclo$7,000 – $9,500
Full lunch per person$8,000 – $15,000
Glass of artisanal chicha$1,500 – $3,000

How to choose a restaurant in Pomaire

In Pomaire there are more than 20 restaurants, most concentrated on the main street (Roberto Bravo / San Antonio) and around it. Almost all offer a very similar menu of traditional Chilean cuisine, so the choice usually depends on the atmosphere, the speed and how busy it is:

  • Traditional restaurants on the main street: The best known and most visited, with the giant empanada and a full menu. They fill up first on weekends.
  • Family-run spots and small eateries: More affordable and authentic, often run by the same family. Good value for money.
  • Restaurants with a patio or terrace: Ideal for going with children or in large groups, with more space.
Local tip: Look at where the pomairinos themselves and the regulars eat. A place full of locals is usually a better sign than one full only of passing tourists.

Opening hours and the best times to eat

Most restaurants open from Tuesday to Sunday, roughly between 11:00 and 18:00–19:00. On Mondays some places close or reduce their hours.

The busiest point is the weekend lunch between 13:00 and 14:30. If you want to avoid waits and find a table calmly, have lunch before 12:30 or after 15:00.

Tips for eating in Pomaire

  1. Bring cash: The large restaurants accept cards, but many small places only take cash.
  2. Share the giant empanada: It is huge; ideal for two people if you are also going to order another dish.
  3. Arrive early on weekends: From 13:00 everything fills up. Before 12:30 you will find a table without a problem.
  4. Ask for the dish of the day: It is usually the freshest and best-priced option.
  5. Leave room for dessert: Try the sopaipillas pasadas or the homemade rice pudding.

Frequently asked questions about where to eat in Pomaire

How much does the giant empanada of Pomaire cost?

The giant empanada, which weighs close to one kilo, costs approximately between $6,000 and $7,000 CLP depending on the restaurant and the filling. A regular baked empanada costs between $3,500 and $5,000 CLP.

Do restaurants in Pomaire accept cards?

Most large restaurants accept cards and have a POS terminal, but many small places only take cash. It is best to bring cash just in case.

Are there vegetarian options in Pomaire?

Yes, although the cuisine is mainly meat-based. You can find cheese empanadas, pastel de choclo (ask for it without meat), humitas and salads. It is best to ask at the venue.

How to Get to Pomaire from Santiago

Last updated: September 2026 | Reading time: 6 minutes

Pomaire is just 50 kilometres west of Santiago, in the district of Melipilla (Metropolitan Region), which makes it one of the most accessible day trips from the capital. Here we explain all the ways to get there, with times, costs and practical tips updated to 2026.

In this guide

  • How to get there by car
  • How to get there by bus / public transport
  • How to get there on an organised tour
  • Times and costs compared
  • Parking when you arrive
  • Frequently asked questions

How to get there by car

The most comfortable and fastest way to reach Pomaire is by car via the Autopista del Sol (Route 78), the road that connects Santiago with San Antonio.

  1. From Santiago, get on the Autopista del Sol (Route 78) heading west (towards San Antonio).
  2. Continue along the motorway and take the exit to Pomaire, signposted at approximately km 50.
  3. Follow the signs to the centre of the village, where the workshops, restaurants and shops are concentrated.
  4. Park on the main street or at the northern entrance of the village.

The trip from central Santiago takes approximately 50 minutes without traffic. The motorway is a toll road (~$3,800 CLP each way).

Tip: If you go on a weekend, leave before 9:00 AM. Between 9:00 and 11:00 the motorway gets congested and the trip can take up to 1 hour and 15 minutes.

How to get there by bus / public transport

Getting there by public transport requires a connection, but it is entirely feasible and affordable:

  1. Take an intercity bus to Melipilla at the Terminal San Borja, located next to the Estación Central metro. The fare is around $2,500 CLP.
  2. On arriving in Melipilla, take a shared taxi (colectivo) or local bus to Pomaire (~15 minutes, ~$800 CLP). They run frequently during the day.
  3. Some routes from Melipilla go directly through Pomaire: ask the driver whether the route includes the stop in the village.
Tip: The last return from Melipilla to Santiago is usually in the late afternoon. Check the return times beforehand so you don't get stranded, especially in winter when it gets dark earlier.

How to get there on an organised tour

If you prefer not to drive or connect transport, several tour agencies in Santiago offer half-day tours to Pomaire that include round-trip transport, a guide and free time to have lunch and shop. Prices range from $25,000 to $45,000 CLP per person, depending on the agency and what is included.

Times and costs compared

MeansApprox. timeCost per person (round trip)
Own car50 min~$7,600 tolls + fuel
Bus + colectivo1 h 15 min~$6,600 CLP
Organised tourHalf day$25,000 – $45,000 CLP

Parking when you arrive

Pomaire is a small village that is best explored on foot. When you arrive by car you can park at:

  • Main street: Free on-street parking, more limited on weekends.
  • Northern entrance of the village: A large lot with space for cars and buses.
  • Private car parks: Some restaurants offer parking for their customers.

See more details in our guide to parking in Pomaire.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a direct bus from Santiago to Pomaire?

There is usually no direct bus. The common way is to take a bus to Melipilla from the Terminal San Borja and from there a colectivo or local bus to Pomaire (about 15 minutes).

How much does it cost to get there by public transport?

Around $5,000 to $6,600 CLP round trip per person, adding the bus to Melipilla and the local colectivo.

Frequently Asked Questions about Pomaire

Last updated: September 2026

We have gathered the most common questions from those planning a visit to Pomaire, the most famous pottery village in Chile. Here you will find quick answers about how to get there, opening hours, prices, parking and much more.

How do I get to Pomaire from Santiago?

By car, take the Autopista del Sol (Route 78) heading west and take the exit at km 50 towards Pomaire; the trip takes about 50 minutes. By public transport, take a bus to Melipilla from the Terminal San Borja (Estación Central metro) and from Melipilla a colectivo or local bus to Pomaire. More details in our guide on how to get to Pomaire.

How long does it take to get to Pomaire from Santiago?

By car, about 50 minutes without traffic. On weekend mornings the trip can rise to 1 hour and 15 minutes because of congestion on the motorway.

Is Pomaire open on Mondays?

The village is always open, but on Mondays many workshops and restaurants close or reduce their hours. The best days to visit with everything open are Tuesday to Sunday.

How much does it cost to visit Pomaire?

Walking around the village and entering the workshops is free. A half-day outing costs approximately between $20,000 and $50,000 CLP per person, including lunch, transport and a craft souvenir.

Where can I park in Pomaire?

There is free parking on the main street and at the northern entrance of the village, as well as private car parks at some restaurants. On weekends it fills up before 11:00, so it is best to arrive early. See more at parking in Pomaire.

How much time do I need to visit Pomaire?

Half a day (4 to 5 hours) is enough to walk around the workshops, have lunch and shop for crafts. If you want to take it slowly or combine it with the Melipilla Wine Route, you can dedicate the whole day. See our one-day itinerary.

Is Pomaire suitable for children?

Yes, it is a very family-friendly destination. Children enjoy watching the artisans work the clay, some workshops offer classes to make pieces, and there are attractions such as the giant piggy bank. Check our guide to Pomaire with kids.

How much does the giant empanada of Pomaire cost?

The giant empanada, which weighs close to one kilo, costs approximately between $6,000 and $7,000 CLP. A regular baked empanada costs between $3,500 and $5,000 CLP. See the guide to where to eat in Pomaire.

What should I buy in Pomaire?

The most typical thing is clay pottery: piggy banks (from $2,000 CLP), pots and dishes for cooking, tableware, planters and signature decorative pieces. Buying directly from the workshops supports the artisan and is usually cheaper.

Can I pay by card in Pomaire?

The large restaurants accept cards, but many workshops and small shops only take cash. It is recommended to bring cash for craft purchases.

What is the best time to visit Pomaire?

Pomaire can be visited all year round. Spring (September to November) and autumn (March to May) offer pleasant weather and fewer people. In summer there is more atmosphere but more heat and crowds.

Do I have to pay to see the pottery workshops?

No, entering the workshops and watching the artisans work is free. You only pay if you take a pottery class (between $10,000 and $20,000 CLP) or if you buy a piece.

Pomaire in One Day: Full Itinerary from Santiago

Last updated: September 2026 | Reading time: 7 minutes

Pomaire is the perfect day trip from Santiago: culture, crafts and food just 50 minutes from the capital. With this hour-by-hour itinerary you will make the most of your visit to the most famous pottery village in Chile, without leaving anything important out.

In this guide

  • Hour-by-hour itinerary
  • Summary of the day
  • Estimated budget
  • Tips to make the most of the day

Hour-by-hour itinerary

  • 09:00Departure from Santiago. Take the Autopista del Sol (Route 78) early to avoid weekend congestion. See how to get to Pomaire.
  • 10:00Arrival and coffee. Park at the entrance of the village and start with a coffee or sopaipillas while the village wakes up. By this time the workshops are already opening.
  • 10:30Tour of the clay workshops. Walk the main street and go into the workshops to see the artisans work the clay live. Ideal for taking photos and choosing what you will buy later.
  • 12:00Pottery class (optional). Several workshops offer 1-hour experiences where you create your own piece. An ideal activity to do calmly before lunch.
  • 13:00Traditional lunch. Try the famous giant baked empanada and a cazuela served in a clay pot. See where to eat in Pomaire.
  • 14:30The World's Largest Clay Piggy Bank. Visit the giant clay sculpture, one of Pomaire's most photogenic icons.
  • 15:00Pomaire main square. Stroll around the main square and the San Antonio de Padua church, with a craft fair and a family atmosphere.
  • 15:30Craft shopping. Now yes, buy what you chose in the morning: piggy banks, pots, tableware or decorative pieces. Buying at the end avoids carrying fragile clay all day.
  • 16:30Return or extension. Head back to Santiago calmly, or extend the day by visiting the nearby Melipilla Wine Route.
Tip: If you go on a weekday, everything will be quieter and you won't need to get up as early. On weekends, however, it is best to leave before 9:00 to find parking and avoid queues at the restaurants.

Summary of the day

  • Morning: Clay workshops + optional pottery class.
  • Midday: Traditional lunch with a giant empanada.
  • Afternoon: Giant piggy bank, main square and craft shopping.
  • Optional extension: Melipilla Wine Route.

Estimated budget per person

  • Transport (car or bus): ~$5,000 – $7,600 CLP
  • Full lunch: $8,000 – $15,000 CLP
  • Pottery class (optional): $10,000 – $20,000 CLP
  • Craft souvenir: $2,000 – $15,000 CLP
  • Estimated total: $20,000 – $50,000 CLP

Tips to make the most of the day

  1. Arrive early on weekends to park without problems.
  2. Bring cash: many workshops only take cash.
  3. Wear comfortable shoes: the tour is on foot along uneven streets.
  4. Buy at the end of the tour so you don't carry fragile pieces around.
  5. Ask about shipping if you buy large pieces: several workshops deliver to Santiago.

con-ninos.en:
Pomaire with Kids: The Perfect Family Outing near Santiago

Last updated: September 2026 | Reading time: 6 minutes

Pomaire is one of the best family outings near Santiago. Just 50 minutes from the capital, it offers children an entertaining and educational experience: watching the artisans mould the clay, getting their hands into the mud, meeting the giant piggy bank and eating well in a calm, open-air atmosphere. Here we tell you how to make the most of it as a family.

In this guide

  • Activities for children in Pomaire
  • Where to eat with kids
  • Practical tips for going as a family
  • Recommended by age

Activities for children in Pomaire

  • A clay workshop to make their own piece: Several workshops offer classes where children mould their own little piggy bank or vessel. It is the star activity: fun, sensory and with a keepsake to take home.
  • Watching the artisans work: Children are fascinated by seeing how a lump of clay becomes a pot or figure on the wheel. Entering the workshops is free.
  • The World's Largest Clay Piggy Bank: A giant clay sculpture, perfect for family photos and to amaze the little ones.
  • A walk around the square: An open, safe space for children to walk while the adults browse the crafts.
  • Buying a piggy bank: An affordable keepsake (from $2,000 CLP) that children love and teaches them to save.
Tip: Book the pottery class for the morning, when children are fresher and full of energy. Ask at the workshop about the recommended minimum age.

Where to eat with kids

Many restaurants in Pomaire have a patio or terrace and plenty of space, which makes them comfortable for going with children. The portions are generous, so a giant empanada can be enough to share among several people. There are also simple options that tend to please the youngest, such as cheese empanadas or humitas.

Check our complete guide to where to eat in Pomaire to choose the best place.

Practical tips for going as a family

  1. Flat streets, on foot: The village is explored on foot along flat streets, comfortable for a stroller (although the surface can be uneven in some stretches).
  2. Arrive early: Especially on weekends, to park nearby and avoid walking a lot with tired children.
  3. Bring water and sun protection: In summer the sun is strong and there is little shade on the main street.
  4. Clothes that can get dirty: If they are going to do a clay workshop, the mud stains! Bring a change of clothes or an apron.
  5. Cash on hand: For the children's quick purchases at the stalls.

Recommended by age

  • Babies and under 3: The walk and the square work well; the clay workshop is better left for later.
  • 4 to 10 years: The ideal age for the pottery workshop and to enjoy the giant piggy bank and the shops.
  • Pre-teens and teenagers: They enjoy creating more elaborate pieces and exploring the village with more independence.
Full-day idea: Combine Pomaire with a long lunch and, if there is energy left, a short stroll around the rural surroundings of Melipilla. A complete family plan without going far from Santiago.
